issue_context.title: dry-run returns unwanted metadata fields
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Running kubectl create with dry-run returns unwanted uid metadata field, as well as a generated name when using generateName.

This is inconsistent with the expectations as defined in [KEP 576](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/576-dry-run/README.md#generated-values) which states

```
The UID and the generated name would have a different value in a dry-run and non-dry-run creation. These values will be left empty when performing a dry-run.
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected uid, and a generated name to be empty when using the dry-run create option.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
cat <<EOF > /tmp/d.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  generateName: foo-
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      test: foo
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        test: foo
    spec:
      containers:
        - command:
            - sleep
            - inf
          image: busybox:latest
          name: sleeper
EOF

kubectl create -f /tmp/d.yaml --dry-run=server -o yaml
```

Expected metadata:
```
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2021-12-16T21:24:32Z"
  generateName: foo-
  generation: 1
  namespace: default
```

Actual metadata:
```
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2021-12-16T21:24:32Z"
  generateName: foo-
  generation: 1
  name: foo-f8jql
  namespace: default
  uid: 3d26f113-01a0-491a-a4e4-4b77f8be5ce1
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

review_comments: this is specific to create, so should be named appropriately so it doesn't accidentally get called for update/delete/patch dry-run cases

```suggestion
	// If resourceVersion is a non-empty string, then non-dry-run-creation will fail. To allow non-dry-run creation of the object returned by dry-run creation, we set the resourceVersion to an empty string.
	newObjMeta.SetResourceVersion("")
```
Reworded as I was getting confused switching back and forth between dry-run and non-dry-run. WDYT?
I'm not sure about this bit... isn't the case where the storage generated the name indistinguishable from a case where the user posted an object containing both `name` and `generateName`?
Drat. You're right. That complicates things a ton.
was this ever resolved in a follow up?
opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109174. we should revert this bit in 1.24 to match 1.23 behavior rather than regress
why is this done here and not in DryRunnableStorage#Create?
Because then you have to carry the dry-run flag through an amazing number of validation layers. I started out that way but it spiraled out of control very quickly.
Nice refactor! :heart:

```suggestion
	// If UID is a non-empty string, then non-dry-run-creation will fail. To allow non-dry-run creation of the object returned by dry-run creation, we set UID to an empty string.
	newObjMeta.SetUID("")
```
Reworded as I was getting confused switching back and forth between dry-run and non-dry-run. WDYT?

if we can't get an Accessor from the input or output objects, I think we should no-op rather than error

alternatively, if we think we should *always* be able to get these, we should change the signature to take oldObj, newObj accessors
same question here, was this ever resolved in a follow up?

> output cannot be used to create a resource

same question about whether this is expected/encouraged (I don't think it is / should be)
I expected it is expected because it's documented that way in the KEP.

> allow the output to be used to create resources

is this a thing we expect/encourage? I would have expected someone to re-post what they sent in the dry-run create request, rather than loop-back the server output of the dry-run create request. Doing the latter won't work like you expect for types that allocate values like service
Yeah, that's true. Also in general, you wouldn't want to apply the default values.

```suggestion
		// If both generateName and name are non-empty strings, then non-dry-run creation will fail. To allow non-dry-run creation of the object returned by dry-run creation, we set name to an empty string.
		newObjMeta.SetName("")
```
I think this text better explains. WDYT?
